rv.q: In his aptly named Amaze, Jamie Allan relates his story of being raised by loving parents, discovering his life’s passion at an early age, and being lucky enough to pursue it and master it. The show is a touching coming-of-age tale, mixing humor and poignancy to wonderful effect, delivered with charm and wit.
Themed in the 1980s, Amaze takes us back to Allan’s formative years, what lead him to become a magician. It’s charming. He’s charming.
Tricks aside, Allan is a charming and warm performer who welcomes the audience into sharing his love of this form of escapism.
I appreciated Amaze more than being enraptured.
Directed by Jonathan Goodwin, Jamie Allan’s Amaze is astonishing.
If you love illusions, you will not want to miss Jamie Allan’s AMAZE!
This is a show that caters to everyone in the family, and it’s a show that certainly lives up to its ambitious title.
I did not leave with my jaw dropped but with a flicker of childhood wonder reignited, and a loving nod to the memories and mentors that taught me to find the extraordinary in the everyday.

cn.t: Critics praise this charming magic show for blending skillful illusions with heartfelt storytelling about Allan's childhood and parents. While some find the enchantment occasionally fizzles, most agree it's a delightful, family-friendly experience.
